transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-06-07 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Evan Brooks (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (SkyForge CTO), Liam O'Connor (SkyForge DevOps), Sofia Alvarez (SkyForge Product), Marcus Yuan (SkyForge Security)

Summary: Quick kickoff for onboarding SkyForge Studios onto Redwood platform (hosted -> dedicated pilot -> VPC private demo runway). Align on networking, security artifacts, pilot metrics, and a dry-run timeline.

Agenda:
- Introductions and success criteria (10m)
- Network & security intake (15m)
- Pilot plan: dedicated pool and dry-run (15m)
- Observability and SLOs (10m)
- Next steps & action items (8m)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. i'm Jordan, lead for the SkyForge account here at Redwood. quick round table?
[00:12] Priya: hi all, Priya Nair from SkyForge, CTO. excited, we have a few priorities — latency, cost predictability, and of course security compliance.
[00:22] Jordan: totally, that matches what we saw in the intake form. Maya and Evan will run the onboarding cadence with you.
[00:28] Maya: hi! i'll own the playbook and the runbook for the first 8 weeks. looking to make the pilot frictionless.
[00:35] Evan: and i'm Evan, solutions eng — i'll own the dry-run tests and latency baselining and help with quantization knobs if you pick smaller models.
[00:44] Sofia: quick question — you said "dedicated pool" before, is that the Redwood Dedicated product or a hosted config?
[00:52] Jordan: great call — we're proposing a dedicated reserved pool for your initial traffic to keep latency predictable. that said we can start hosted for early validation and then schedule a dedicated pool carve-out.
[01:03] Liam: how much lead time is that? our infra team needs to plan GPU allocation and the VPC peer.
[01:09] Evan: for a dedicated pool typically 2-3 weeks to provision and validate network paths; dry-run sooner if you use hosted with a canary route.
[01:18] Priya: ok 2-3 weeks is fine. Marcus, our security lead, is on the call — Marcus, anything top-line?
[01:24] Marcus: yeah two asks — SOC2 artifacts and an encryption/KMS story. we need model-key separation and audit logs. also can you clarify retention for KV cache traces?
[01:36] Jordan: absolutely. we'll share our SOC2 scope doc and the KMS integration notes. note the runtime supports customer-managed KMS for on-prem or VPC deployments; for hosted you can opt-in for our managed key or bring-your-own via KMS.
[01:50] Priya: sometimes the docs from vendors are a little vague — can you share specifics like API endpoints and accepted ciphers?
[01:57] Maya: yes, we'll attach a network diagram and the TLS cipher list. expect that in the staging runbook.
[02:05] Sofia: on metrics — we want 95th perc latency under 120ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens). is that realistic?
[02:13] Evan: depends on model and batching behaviour. If you pin a lower-quantized variant and set per-request max batch size to 1 with continued batching off, you can hit mid-100ms on our Dedicated with optimized kernels. If we see tail spikes we have routing policies and fallback to cheaper variants to keep availability.
[02:33] Liam: what's the difference between the "prefix cache" and KV cache? I saw both in the docs but sounds similar.
[02:38] Evan: yeah that's a common confusion — prefix cache is content-level caching where we cache the output for identical prefixes, KV cache is at the key-value attention cache level to speed up autoregressive decoding when you have long context. sometimes transcript shows it as "kay-vee cache" or "K-V cache" — we call it KV.
[02:55] Priya: great, we anticipate a mix of short synchronous prompts and some background batch rerank jobs. we care about cost on rerank.
[03:03] Jordan: for rerank jobs we recommend batching and a quantized reranker to reduce GPU cycles; we'll include batching config suggestions in the Optimize playbook.
[03:12] Marcus: also DLP question — does Redwood persist raw request bodies in logs? we need the option to redact PII server-side.
[03:21] Maya: by default we retain audit logs for operational troubleshooting but we can enable redaction and token-level obfuscation. for Private deployments you keep full control.
[03:29] Liam: on networking — we run transit gateway with strict egress rules; what's the peering flow look like?
[03:36] Evan: two options: 1) VPC peering into Redwood managed subnet with specific CIDRs, or 2) private link-style endpoint if you want no route table changes. both require an allowlist of outbound ports. we'll put the exact CIDRs in the runbook.
[03:49] Sofia: will you help with firewall rules? our infra folks prefer exact entries rather than just "allow redwood".
[03:55] Jordan: yep, we'll send a packet-level checklist.
[03:59] Priya: timeline — we'd like pilot live in prod in ~4 weeks, full rollout in 10 weeks. realistic?
[04:07] Evan: pilot (staged traffic) in 3 weeks is doable if we get traffic profile and network details this week. full rollout depends on your QA cadence but 8-10 weeks is typical.
[04:18] Marcus: can we do an early compliance review before the pilot? I want to review the audit log schema and key rotation policy.
[04:25] Maya: yes, we'll schedule a compliance deep-dive with our security engineer and deliver SOC2 artifacts.
[04:31] Jordan: quick note on billing — pilot usage will be billed at trial rates; dedicated commit pricing can be discussed once we size GPU pool. I'll send a high level cost worksheet.
[04:42] Liam: one more — do you support single-sign-on for admin console and RBAC?
[04:47] Maya: SSO yes (SAML/SSO supported) and RBAC is role-based with team-level scoping. we'll include a step for SSO test users in the runbook.
[04:56] Sofia: any reference customers in gaming / real-time inference?
[04:59] Jordan: we have a couple — i'll share a short case study (anonymized) showing sub-100ms 95th perc on in-game prompts.
[05:08] Priya: perfect, thanks. can you also outline rollback conditions? we want an explicit kill-switch plan if latency or cost exceeds thresholds.
[05:17] Evan: yes rollback playbook: autoscale down, route to hosted fallback, and a manual model downgrade. we'll document specific thresholds e.g., 95th perc > 200ms for 5 minutes triggers automatic fallback.
[05:30] Marcus: last thing — are there network probes or health checks we need to enable from our side?
[05:35] Evan: a simple TCP health at the endpoint and a token-latency probe. we'll provide the script.
[05:41] Jordan: ok let's recap action items and timeline. Maya will send runbook w/ network diagram and SSO steps by 6/10. Evan will produce latency baseline script and test matrix by 6/14. Jordan will share cost worksheet and reference case. SkyForge to provide traffic profile and firewall contacts by 6/9. Marcus to get SOC2 clarifications by 6/12. Dry-run week targeted for 6/21.
[06:04] Priya: thanks everyone, that works. we'll block time with the infra team for the dry-run.
[06:10] Sofia: appreciated, talk soon.
[06:15] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and the runbook.

End of transcript.
